# `multiple-of-changed`

multipleOf changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `multiple-of-changed` (both directions), `multiple-of-changed-in-request`, `multiple-of-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`multipleOf` changed. Whether it narrowed or widened is worked out from the values.

## Why this default

In requests: values valid before may be rejected. In responses: clients may receive values that are not multiples of the old step.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  multiple-of-changed: warn
```

## How to fix

Keep the old step.
